name: Starlink V1.5 (Gen1, post-VisorSat)
note: Parity model for the v1.1 'Starlink' (Gen1) type. The V1.0 chassis without a visor (it blocked the laser links), the nadir face under SpaceX's gen-1 dielectric mirror film, dark-red inter-cell material; the array tracks the Sun about its hinge (normal on-station operation). Body frame: +Z nadir, +X toward the Sun's azimuth. Sanity check: Mallama & Respler 2022's Post-VisorSat phase function (no published mean).

sources.value: the V1.0 bus: 1.3 x 2.8 m, 0.2 m thick, polished aluminium
sources.source: Same chassis as starlink_v1_0.json (its sources: McDowell, planet4589.org/astro/starsim; Cole 2021 arXiv:2107.06026).

sources.subject: nadir_mirror_film
sources.value: gen-1 dielectric mirror film over the whole nadir face
sources.source: SpaceX, 'Brightness Mitigation Best Practices for Satellite Operators' (2022): no visor ('the material did block the laser links'), 'RF-transparent mirror films' instead - 'Current Starlink v1.5 satellites use the Gen1 dielectric mirrors' - and 'a darker material between the solar cells', 'now pigmented dark red'. Coverage of the entire base (antennas included - the film is RF-transparent) and the film's reflectance (dielectric_mirror_gen1 preset) are estimates.

sources.subject: solar_array
sources.value: one 2.8 x 8.1 m array, dark-red inter-cell material
sources.source: Same chassis as starlink_v1_0.json (its sources: McDowell, planet4589.org/astro/starsim; Cole 2021 arXiv:2107.06026); SpaceX, 'Brightness Mitigation Best Practices for Satellite Operators' (2022): no visor ('the material did block the laser links'), 'RF-transparent mirror films' instead - 'Current Starlink v1.5 satellites use the Gen1 dielectric mirrors' - and 'a darker material between the solar cells', 'now pigmented dark red'. The solar_cell preset's albedo (0.02) was calibrated on VisorSat (M8).

sources.subject: bus
sources.value: base to nadir, yawed so the array's hinge axis lies across the Sun
sources.source: Normal on-station operation (array facing the Sun) - the Post-VisorSat era before the knife-edge roll mitigation (Mallama & Respler 2023, 'Roll angle adjustment dims Starlink satellites'). Not published by SpaceX; checked against Mallama & Respler 2022 (arXiv:2210.17268): Post-VisorSat phase function m1000 = 3.944 + 0.06893 phi - 0.0004089 phi^2 (Table 1), characteristic magnitude 5.5 at 72 deg and 550 km.

sources.subject: array
sources.value: the array turns about its hinge to face the Sun

sources.subject: bus_metal
sources.source: Same chassis as starlink_v1_0.json (its sources: McDowell, planet4589.org/astro/starsim; Cole 2021 arXiv:2107.06026).

sources.subject: array_backsheet_gen1
sources.value: white translucent backsheet: albedo 0.5 (estimate), diffuse transmission 0.03 (fitted)
sources.source: SpaceX (2022): the back of a solar array 'can be lit up by the sun like a lampshade' - fixed on the V2 with 'an opaque pigment for the solar backsheet', i.e. Gen1 backsheets were translucent. Transmission FITTED to Mallama & Respler 2022 (arXiv:2210.17268): Post-VisorSat phase function m1000 = 3.944 + 0.06893 phi - 0.0004089 phi^2 (Table 1), characteristic magnitude 5.5 at 72 deg and 550 km: the 100-160 deg bins (an opaque back left them 2.7-3.9 mag too faint; T = 0.03 puts them within 0.6); metric = the paper's phase function, 5000 samples seed 1 of a Mallama/Respler-sited 550 km campaign (2026-09-24). Held out: nothing (no published mean or per-pass data).
